title: Where should AI enter your enquiry workflow?
summary: Use a sales enquiry to separate useful AI assistance from the actions a person should own.

sections.title: Begin with the handover that fails
paragraphs: A customer asks for a quotation on WhatsApp. Someone copies the message into a spreadsheet, someone else replies by email, and nobody records who will follow up. Adding an AI reply to this process leaves the ownership problem in place.

Before introducing an agent, write down the source of the enquiry, the customer record it should match, the person responsible and the next action. Use a real example from your team, with personal details removed, to test the proposed journey.

sections.title: Separate preparation from commitment
paragraphs: A useful first scope might allow AI to summarise the request, retrieve approved product information and prepare a reply. The sales owner checks the requirement and approves the response. Prices, delivery commitments and unusual requests remain with the responsible person.

rows: Enquiry linked to a customer record
Summary and reply draft using approved information
Next task and due date recorded

sections.title: Give exceptions somewhere to go
paragraphs: Test an incomplete request, a duplicate contact, a missing document and a disconnected CRM. Each case needs a visible outcome. A workflow that cannot complete the task should preserve the useful context and route the exception to a person.

NatChat can be considered for WhatsApp conversations and NatiVox for an appropriate voice workflow. Their role follows the agreed channel, account access and process; a product name alone does not define the implementation.

sections.title: Review a small pilot before expanding
items: Check whether the summary preserves the customer’s actual request.
Count drafts that need material correction, not just messages produced.
Review owner assignment, outstanding tasks and missed handovers.
Compare completion time and review effort with the current process.
paragraphs: Begin with one bounded workflow. Expand when the team can explain the result, handle the exceptions and maintain the information the agent uses.

title: SEO, AEO and GEO: what should your business do first?
summary: Start with the page, the customer’s question and the evidence behind your answer. Avoid treating AI visibility as a guaranteed placement.

sections.title: Keep the customer’s question in view
paragraphs: A customer comparing two suppliers needs to understand what each supplier does, whether the offer fits and how to ask a useful question. A page full of broad claims about innovation gives that customer little help.

Choose one service page. Write down the questions your sales or support team actually receives. Identify which answers the page already provides and which require information from someone inside the business.

sections.title: Understand the terminology
paragraphs: SEO concerns search visibility. AEO and GEO are commonly used for work focused on answers and generative search experiences. Google’s guidance treats optimisation for its generative features as part of the broader search experience, rather than a separate route around its search systems.

For Google Search, there is no special AI schema or required llms.txt file that secures inclusion. Useful, distinctive content and sound search foundations remain relevant. No page update can promise a citation or placement in an AI answer.

sections.title: Build an evidence-led page brief

rows: A clear explanation of who the service helps
What do I need to provide?
A real enquiry route and response owner
A visible, usable call to action

paragraphs: Have the person who owns the service review the answers. Do not invent certifications, customer outcomes or delivery promises to make the page appear more persuasive.

sections.title: Check the technical foundations and the journey
paragraphs: Review the page title, main topic, metadata, language, internal links and any indexing instructions. Check the live page on a phone and follow its enquiry route. An accurate answer is less useful if the contact button leads to a missing page.

Use the on-page HTML review to identify evidence worth inspecting, and Google PageSpeed for its performance diagnostics. Neither result is a forecast of rankings, leads or AI citations. Review actual search and enquiry information over time, with the changes and measurement limits recorded.

title: Measure automation with time recovered and work completed
summary: A small worked example shows why task coverage, review effort and operating costs belong in the same calculation.

sections.title: Record the baseline before changing the work
paragraphs: Choose a repeatable task and observe how it is handled today. Record the number of cases, the time spent, the people involved and the corrections needed. Separate waiting time from active work so the comparison answers a clear question.
A statement such as ‘we automated half the work’ does not tell you how much effort remains. Some cases still need manual handling, and automated outputs may require review.

sections.title: Include the review time
paragraphs: Consider an illustrative team with 100 eligible task hours per month. A proposed workflow covers 50% of those hours. If review consumes 20% of the covered hours, it recovers 40 hours: 50 covered hours minus 10 review hours.

At an entered labour value of ₹500 per hour, those recovered hours are worth ₹20,000 in the model. With ₹3,000 of monthly operating costs, the modelled monthly net benefit is ₹17,000. These are example assumptions, not a client result.

sections.title: Do not confuse capacity with cash
paragraphs: Recovered time is useful capacity. It becomes a cash saving only if actual costs fall. If the team uses the time to serve more customers, measure that additional work separately. Avoid adding both the same staff-time value and the full value of new sales without checking for double counting.
Include setup, software, model usage, maintenance and exception handling where they apply. Keep the assumptions visible so another team member can challenge them.

sections.title: Compare the model with a pilot
items: Sample completed work for accuracy and completeness.
Record manual fallbacks and the time spent resolving them.
Compare review effort with the assumption used in the calculator.
Review recurring costs and whether recovered capacity was actually used.
paragraphs: Use the calculators to organise the question. Use observed work to decide whether the proposed workflow deserves a wider rollout.

title: Five fields that make a customer follow-up easier to own
summary: A record becomes useful when it explains the request, the responsible person and the next action.

sections.title: Design the record around the next conversation
paragraphs: A contact name and a phone number tell you who the customer is. They do not explain why the customer contacted you or what your team agreed to do. Start with the information someone needs to continue the conversation without asking the customer to repeat everything.

sections.title: Make these five items visible

rows: Which record and conversation this request belongs to
The customer’s actual need, with relevant context
The person responsible for the next step
A specific task that someone can complete
When the task should happen or be checked

paragraphs: For an illustrative enquiry about office furniture, ‘follow up’ is too vague. ‘Priya to share the approved chair specifications by Thursday’ gives the next person a clearer task. The date and commitment must come from the actual conversation.

sections.title: Use status to explain progress
paragraphs: A stage such as ‘qualified’ should mean something your team can describe. Agree what information is required to enter the stage and what action moves the enquiry forward. Keep appointment requests and support cases distinct where their owners and next steps differ.

If an automation assigns the owner or prepares a reminder, test what happens when the owner is unavailable or a required field is missing. An exception should reach a person instead of disappearing into an activity log.

sections.title: Review the open work together
items: Which requests do not have an owner?
Which next actions are overdue or unclear?
Which records lack enough context for a useful reply?
paragraphs: Begin with the record your team can maintain consistently. Add fields when they support a real decision, handover or reporting need. A larger database is not automatically a clearer working process.
